title: Unit-scaling row classes are invariant under ring isomorphism
statement: For any commutative rings R and S and any ring isomorphism e:R≃S, define P(A), for each commutative ring A, as the quotient of {(r,s)∈A² | ∃x,y∈A, xr+ys=1} by the relation (r,s)∼(r',s') iff some unit u∈Aˣ satisfies ur=r' and us=s'. Then there exists an equivalence P(R)≃P(S). No finiteness or nontriviality assumption on either ring is required.
lean_statement: ∀ (R S : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing S], (R ≃+* S) → let P := fun (A : Type) [CommRing A] => Quot (fun v w : {v : A × A // ∃ x y : A, x * v.1 + y * v.2 = 1} => ∃ u : Aˣ, (u : A) * v.1.1 = w.1.1 ∧ (u : A) * v.1.2 = w.1.2); Nonempty (P R ≃ P S)
